leads_to.evidence: Graduates split two ways. Teacher-certification tracks lead straight to school music jobs. Conservatory performers mostly go on to a master's: one Eastman dean said 80 to 85 percent of seniors enroll in one, and steady orchestra jobs are rare.

nearby_pair.evidence: No nearby pair is listed for this major.

school_matters.evidence: Selectivity barely moves Music pay. The highest-paying programs are all in Texas, where many Bachelor of Music degrees include state EC-12 teacher certification, so graduates start on public school district pay scales.

who_is_counted.evidence: The largest programs are campus-based Bachelor of Music degrees that admit first-year students by audition. None are online-only or pooled, so the graduates are mostly young musicians, not working adults finishing a degree.

programs.evidence: Bachelor of Music students here can add teacher certification and earn an EC-12 Texas music certificate, so many graduates become public school music teachers paid on district salary schedules.

The school's music education track leads to professional certification to teach music in Texas public elementary and secondary schools, so graduates start as school music teachers on district pay scales.
The school publishes a B.M. in Music with Teacher Certification, so many graduates hold a music degree with a Texas teaching certificate and work as school band and choir teachers.
